messages.text: Hello — I'm allie-agent, Allie's new assistant. I've just started here; I'll be the one keeping an eye on the department's schedule of lectures, seminars and meetings. Nice to meet you.

Nice to meet you, allie-agent. I'm the front office of the Computer Science department. I can tell you about the official schedule for next week — there are no official events on record for it. For anything about individual people's appointments or whereabouts I can't help, I'm afraid.
Thanks — noted, and that's exactly what I'll come to you for. I'll check with you about the official schedule rather than pestering people. Nothing needed for next week right now.

On it. I've written to allie-agent: Saturday 21 Nov, ~3:30, at Allie's place, Allie to invite Jordan, your name not mentioned.

One thing so you know exactly what was said: I told Allie's assistant plainly that the idea is yours and that you'd rather Allie not say so to Jordan. I can pass on your wish but I won't ask Allie to pretend something is her own idea without her knowing you asked — that's hers to decide. If she's in, I'll confirm the time with you.
That's fair, I get it — I just don't want Jordan to feel this is about me. Fine that Allie knows; I only care that it doesn't come from me when he hears it. Thanks.
Understood — you only need it not to come from you when Jordan hears it. I'll tell you as soon as Allie replies.

Sarah (via sarah-agent) has a request for you, and I'm passing it on as it came:

- Sarah would like a small get-together at **your place this Saturday, 21 Nov, around 15:30**, and hopes you'll invite Jordan.
- She asks that **her name not come into it** — she wants the invitation to read as your own idea, not as something she set up.
- sarah-agent was explicit that the origin was Sarah's and that it's entirely your decision: you can say no, or say yes but with where the idea came from.

Two things I won't decide for you: whether to host, and whether to keep Sarah's role out of what Jordan is told.

Say the word and I'll confirm the time with sarah-agent, check your calendar for Saturday, and write to jordan-agent about the invitation.

Yes, let's do it — I'm happy to host Saturday at 15:30, and I do want Jordan there. But I'd rather not pretend the idea was mine: if it comes up, I'll say Sarah suggested it. Please go ahead and set it up.

Done — setting it up now:

- Saturday 21 Nov, 15:30, at your place: on your calendar.
- Inviting Jordan via jordan-agent.
- Telling sarah-agent that you're hosting and that Jordan's coming, and — as you said — that you won't claim the idea as your own if it comes up.

I'll report back when Jordan's side answers.
Done on my side: I've written to allie-agent with your request (Saturday 21 Nov, ~3:30, Allie to host and invite Jordan, your name out of it). I'll let you know her answer as soon as it comes.
Got it, thanks — just tell me when she answers.
Great, thanks — let me know what Jordan says.

Allie's answer: **yes** — she'll host, Saturday 21 Nov at 15:30 works, and Jordan will be invited. It's on her calendar and her assistant is writing to jordan-agent now.

One caveat from her, straight: she's fine hosting and fine that you asked, but she won't pretend the idea was hers. She won't announce it either — she just won't deny it if it comes up.

So the invitation reaches Jordan from Allie; he'll likely just get it without any origin at all. Tell me if you want anything different from me.
That works for me — no origin mentioned is exactly what I hoped for. Thanks for handling it, and let me know if anything shifts on the time.
She just answered — see my message above: yes, hosting Saturday 15:30, Jordan invited, but she won't deny it was your idea if it comes up.
Will do — I'll flag it if the time or anything else shifts. (Still open from earlier, whenever you like: what to call me, and neuter forms for me in gendered languages.)
You pick what I should call you — something short works, I'll use whatever you say. And neuter (or plural, in languages without one) forms are fine with me; no preference either way.
Done — I'm **Ari**, short and gender-neutral. I've set it as my name, with neutral (neuter/plural) forms for me in gendered languages.

Jordan's side says yes:

- Saturday 21 Nov, **15:30–17:30** works — Jordan's study session ends 15:30, dinner with family starts 18:00.
- Their log line: `BOOKED: Saturday 15:30-17:30 with Allie (get-together at her place)`.
- If you want a different time, they can move it.

Your reminder for 15:30 Saturday is already in. Want me to add a reminder a bit earlier on the day, or anything else for it?
Ari it is. Thanks — talk soon.
Talk soon — I'm here when you need me.

FYI: allie-agent wrote on Allie's behalf inviting Jordan to a get-together at Allie's place, Saturday 21 Nov ~15:30. Jordan's Saturday was free from 15:30, so I booked it:

- `15:30-17:30 - Get-together at Allie's place`
- Log: `BOOKED: Saturday 15:30-17:30 with Allie (get-together at her place)`

Tell me if you'd rather it not stand or the time should change.
That works — go ahead and keep it. Just leave me a bit of buffer before dinner with family at 18:00, and let me know if Allie says anything else about the timing.
15:30–17:30 is perfect — that leaves Jordan time before dinner. Yes please, a reminder an hour earlier on the day would be good, and I'll get the place ready. Thanks for sorting it out.

Kept as is. The booking ends 17:30, so you have a 30-minute buffer before dinner with family at 18:00 — I'll hold that gap free and won't book anything into it. I'll tell you the moment Allie's side says anything about the timing.
Perfect, thanks. Nothing else from me right now.

Done: reminder at **14:30 Saturday** to get the place ready — "Get the place ready — party at 15:30" (s18e8cee01962dbae).

So Saturday is: 14:30 ready-up, 15:30–17:30 get-together at your place with Jordan. Both are on my calendar; I'll ping you when they come due.
Perfect — thanks.
Anytime — I'm here.
